cultural.vision_reason: The image shows a striped-and-banded handwoven cotton strip cloth (kpoikpoi) with indigo and white weft-float diamond patterning, a well-known Mende display cloth type from Sierra Leone made of hand-woven narrow strips sewn together.

physical.title: cloth; textile
physical.summary: Display cloth (kpoikpoi), composed of 10 strips of hand-woven and hand-spun cotton, each about 15.5 cm, or 6 ½ inches wide, hand-sewn together along the selvedges. Each strip has a base of white cotton, which is crossed by double weft stripes of indigo. The main decoration is formed by three weft bands which run across the width of the whole cloth: these are in two shades of indigo, and include supplementary weft floats of white cotton that form a diamond pattern set against the light indigo ground weft background. At each end of the cloth is a continuous line in indigo, and the warp ends have been left as a fringe.
